prompt: wget time-stamping Content-Length size mismatch behavior
answer:
With Wget’s time-stamping option (`-N`), a `Content-Length` mismatch normally causes the remote file to be downloaded regardless of the timestamps.

However, when Wget uses `If-Modified-Since`, a server may respond with `304 Not Modified`; that response does not provide the file size, so Wget cannot perform the size comparison and may incorrectly skip the download. Using `--no-if-modified-since` makes Wget issue a `HEAD` request to obtain both the timestamp and size.

If a server sends an incorrect `Content-Length`, use `--ignore-length`; otherwise Wget may think the document was not completely retrieved.
